meta_description: Open source platform for operating and billing Swiss (v)ZEV energy communities — from quarter-hourly meter data to a paid, QR-bill invoice.
hero_eyebrow: Open source · Swiss ZEV & vZEV · self-hosted · AGPL-3.0
hero_title: From quarter-hourly meter data to a paid invoice.
hero_lede: Import the load curves, split the solar between participants per 15-minute interval, price it against your tariffs, send a QR-bill invoice. I wrote it to bill my own ZEV, and put it out in case it is useful for yours.
flow_aria: Energy flow for one quarter. Of 1888.85 kWh produced on site, 625.8 kWh is used locally and 1263.05 kWh is exported to the grid. A further 738.9 kWh is imported from the grid, bringing local consumption to 1364.7 kWh and the self-consumption rate to 33.1 percent.
flow_note: The same split the billing engine performs — min(production, consumption) per 15-minute interval — is what every invoice line is derived from.
features_lede: Billing a ZEV is easy for one month. It gets harder when last year's tariff still has to exist, when someone who moved out in March has to be billed for March, and when the invoice has to be something a neighbour accepts without asking for the spreadsheet behind it.
f1_text: The formats Swiss utilities actually send, plus whatever your own meter exports.
f1_li1: CSV and Excel with configurable column mapping, plus SDAT-CH for utility workflows
f1_li2: Preview-based validation with a per-row import protocol
f1_li3: Data-quality checks for gaps, duplicates and implausible readings
f1_li4: Consumption and production analysis by period or daily profile
f2_text: Each interval is priced with the tariff version that was valid at that timestamp. Nothing is averaged over the month.
f2_li1: Versioned tariffs with high/low bands, seasonal periods and validity windows
f2_li2: Dynamic price series, including the BFE reference market price
f2_li3: Import a grid operator's machine-readable tariff file (Art. 7b StromVV)
f2_li4: Per-timestamp local-pool split across every participant
f3_text: Invoices render as PDF/A-3b with a QR-bill payment slip, and move through draft, approved, sent, paid. Cancelling keeps the document and its number rather than deleting the row. Annual statements and participation contracts come out of the same renderer, and every issued version is kept as it was sent.
f4_text: Admins, ZEV owners and participants each get their own view of the same data. Assignments between participants and metering points carry validity dates, so someone moving out on 15 March is billed to 15 March.
f5_text: Estimates savings, payback, ROI and NPV for a planned community. If you already run one, it can prefill from its participants and measured self-consumption.
f6_title: Built to be run by one person
f6_li1: Audit log across every privileged action, scoped to what you may see
f6_li2: Asynchronous email delivery with per-invoice history and retry
f6_li3: API keys for scripting, with read-only scope and their own rate budget
f6_li4: Export or move a whole community between instances as a versioned archive
screens_lede: From the demo community that ships with the project, seeded with one command.
s1_text: Each period shows the action it needs, so you start on the work instead of going looking for it. The period that is still collecting data just says so.
s1_alt: OpenZEV overview screen listing billing periods by status, each with its next action
s2_text: Production, consumption, self-consumption and grid exchange for the selected period, with a Sankey diagram tracing every kWh from producer to participant. Filter by participant or change the resolution down to the interval.
s2_alt: Energy balance screen with KPI tiles and a Sankey diagram of energy flow between producer, participants and the grid
s3_text: Every invoice for the period with its metering completeness, status, total and PDF state, plus batch actions for the steps you would otherwise repeat once per household.
s3_alt: Billing screen listing each participant's invoice with status badges, totals and batch actions
s4_title: Every tariff change is a new version
s4_text: A tariff is a series of versions, each with its own bands and validity window. An invoice raised last year still prices at last year's rate, and the chart shows when each change took effect.
s4_alt: Tariff detail drawer showing version history, a price history chart and the high and low tariff bands
qs_lede: Pick the one that matches where you want it to live. All three pull prebuilt images from GHCR.
p1_text: Starts the stack and seeds a full community — participants, meters, tariffs and readings — so there is something to look at.
p2_text: The full stack — frontend, API, Celery worker and beat, PostgreSQL and Redis — with no demo data.
p3_text: The chart deploys frontend, backend, worker and beat into your cluster with an Ingress and a media PVC. Bring your own PostgreSQL and Redis.
after3_t: PostgreSQL, MariaDB or SQLite via DATABASE_URL
st2_dd: React, TypeScript, Vite, React Query, i18next
st3_dd: Celery worker and beat on Redis
st5_dd: OpenAPI schema with Swagger and ReDoc
st6_dd: Docker Compose, or Helm on Kubernetes
st7_dd: run it, change it, host it. If you offer a modified version to others over a network, they get the source too.
note_title: Read this before you bill someone with it
note_p1: I built OpenZEV to run my own ZEV, and I share it as-is, with no warranty. It suits people who enjoy running their own stack. Check your imports, your tariffs and your invoices before they reach a participant: responsibility for what the numbers say stays with you.
note_p2: It is also built with a lot of AI assistance, down to the specs, ADRs and user documentation. Some choices will look unconventional to an experienced team. That is the trade I made: the project is optimised for learning, experimentation and running one real ZEV, rather than for enterprise process.
